title: Timing: Fast Gray → Binary
constraints: Convert a 32-bit Gray code to binary: `b[i] = g[31] ^ g[30] ^ … ^ g[i]`. Purely combinational.
Timing budget: at most **8 logic levels**. The obvious chain `b[i] = b[i+1] ^ g[i]` is 31 levels deep.
hints: Each b[i] is a suffix XOR, so this is a *prefix computation* (a scan).
Doubling trick: `t = g ^ (g >> 1); t = t ^ (t >> 2); t = t ^ (t >> 4); t = t ^ (t >> 8); t = t ^ (t >> 16);`. That's 5 XOR levels.
The same log-depth scan structure gives fast adders (Kogge-Stone).
